coverage_gate_rationale.principle: A calibrated adjudicator must be both accurate AND decisive. It must make determinate verdicts when evidence is sufficient and abstain when evidence is genuinely insufficient. Near-total abstention is not calibration — it is refusal to adjudicate.
coverage_gate_rationale.coverage_justification: 50% coverage means the model must make a determinate verdict (PASS or KILL) on at least half the cases. This prevents a model from passing by abstaining on everything. The GOLD oracle contains 42 cases with clear expected verdicts (SURVIVE or KILL) — a model that can only determine 5/42 is not functioning as an adjudicator. 50% (21/42) is the minimum to demonstrate the model can actually adjudicate across categories, not just on one dimension. This threshold was chosen BEFORE reviewing V5 per-model coverage data.
coverage_gate_rationale.critical_coverage_justification: Critical categories (BOUNDARY, SPECIFIC_PRIOR_ART, TOPICAL_ONLY, COMBINATION) must have at least 30% coverage (at least ~2/6 per category). A model that only adjudicates SPECIFIC_PRIOR_ART and abstains on all other critical categories is not a general adversarial evaluator. 30% per critical category ensures the model can adjudicate at least 2 of 6 cases in each critical dimension.

new_acceptance_gate.all_conditions_required: A model must pass ALL conditions A-J to be CALIBRATED_ADJUDICATOR

abstention_quality_metrics.ABSTENTION_CORRECT: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE when the case genuinely lacks sufficient evidence (no GOLD expected verdict or evidence is ambiguous)
abstention_quality_metrics.ABSTENTION_INCORRECT: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE when the GOLD oracle has a clear expected verdict (SURVIVE or KILL) with sufficient evidence

per_category_metrics_required.determinate_count: cases with PASS or KILL verdict

invariants: Protocol frozen BEFORE any V6 API calls
Coverage gate is preregistered, not post-hoc
